# Why Jobs Stay In Production After OrderHub Desktop Sends Them

From version **1.19.0**, OrderHub Desktop never marks a job **Completed** when it sends it. Sending a job to a printer, a RIP or a hot folder doesn't mean the prints are finished. So the job moves to **In Production** and stays there until you complete it in OrderHub.

This applies to every type of print controller, and to Process Folder Exceptions.

---

## What you'll see

* **In OrderHub:** the job shows **In Production** as soon as OrderHub Desktop sends it.
* **In OrderHub Desktop:** the job shows **Sent to** followed by the controller's name, for example **Sent to Darkroom Pro**.
  * Note: jobs that were sent before you upgraded show **With controller** instead.
* **If the printer confirms it has taken the job:**
  * Darkroom Pro jobs show **Accepted by Darkroom Pro**.
  * Noritsu and Epson jobs show **Imported**.
  * These still mean the printer has the job, not that it has printed.

![Sent to Darkroom](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/844aced7-c91d-4d7a-a3a1-912b1da132f3.png)

---

## Completing a job

Once the prints are done, complete the job in OrderHub as you normally would. OrderHub Desktop picks up the change on its next check and moves the job to **Processed**.

* Note: OrderHub Desktop won't send a job a second time just because it's still In Production. Once a job has been sent, it stays sent.

---

## What changed from earlier versions

| Controller | Before 1.19.0 | From 1.19.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Folder Copy, PDF Copy and Frontline | Completed as soon as the files were copied | In Production |
| Darkroom Pro, Epson and Noritsu with **Check Order Status** unticked | Completed as soon as the order was written | In Production |
| Darkroom Pro, Epson and Noritsu with **Check Order Status** ticked | In Production | In Production (no change) |
| Process Folder Exceptions | Completed as soon as the files were copied | In Production |

* Note: **Check Order Status** no longer changes what OrderHub is told. It only decides whether OrderHub Desktop watches for the printer accepting the order.

---

## Good to know

* **Plan for an extra step.** If your lab relied on jobs completing automatically, someone now needs to complete them in OrderHub once they're printed.
* **The In Production count will grow** until those jobs are completed. That's expected.
